newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - BTP/Bund spread to narrow if Italy in ERM.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - BTP/Bund spread to narrow if Italy in ERM.

text.p: Italian bonds look set to outstrip German bunds, with the 10-year yield spread narrowing to around 163 basis points by the end of next week if Italy re-enters the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) at the weekend, said bond strategists and economists polled by Reuters on Friday.
But Italian spread gains after that are likely to slow down, they said. The survey showed average expectations of around 160 basis points by year-end.
Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said in Frankfurt on Friday that Italy had asked for the lira to be readmitted to the grid which it left in 1992.
According to the Maastricht Treaty, Italy must be in the ERM for two years before taking part in a single European currency, due to be introduced in 1999.
The BTP/Bund spread forecasts from the 14 respondents in London, Rome and Milan ranged from 150 to 175 basis points for the end of next week and from 115 to 200 basis points for the end of December.
Most economists saw little upside potential, with much of the good news already discounted in the markets and profit-taking expected to kick in.
"The upside is still limited...so much optimism has been built in already," said Phyllis Reed, European bond strategist at BZW in London. "Investors are starting to look to take profits on this."
